answers.answer: In London Season attrition, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card, add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5 or more retires the officeholder. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return that card's fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may each take or discard one card from the London Season display. Select in descending order of actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with more total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a selected or discarded card during selection; if the display empties, immediately skip every remaining eligible player. At the end discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies; unused pensioners do not carry over.

At the start of the Family phase, check the opportunity marker's location; a main action may be taken twice only if the marker already matched that chosen action at phase start. After choosing, place or move the marker onto that action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may then grant an extra action; that extra action is not doubled and does not move the marker. Enlist Writer places a member in any Presidency's Writers box. If at least four offices are vacant, it adds one additional writer once that turn. With the marker already on Enlist Writer and four vacant offices, the doubled main action can place two writers plus the one-time extra writer, three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family phase; Family action — Enlist Writer

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant from the Stock Exchange queue into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Applicants moved to Court are then Company shares. If Debt is exhausted while applicants remain, slide those applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share requires paying its printed queue-space cost to the bank; the initial purchase money does not go to Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family action — Seek Share; New Company shares

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the back of each office card. The designated hirer chooses a candidate, who moves into the office, and that member's owner receives the office card. For an ordinary hire of a member from the hirer's own family, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, move their fatigue to the new office card and insert their old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism and use their own rules.

The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If nobody receives majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, as a fallback; Nepotism consent is not required. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, from a prize (losing that prize's VP); if this is impossible, there is no Chairman.

For a Company-office success check, first commit resources and pay any check cash from the acting office's treasury to the bank, gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures modify this general procedure. Do not take a dead action that has no effect or chance of success—for example, trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses. The summary specifies no generic destination for resources committed to an attempt beyond paying Company-office check cash to the bank; office-specific procedures govern other outcomes.

The Chairman may borrow up to three Debt freely, adding £5 to Company Balance for each Debt. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and borrowing cannot pass the end of the Debt track. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, subject to the same borrowing limits and consent.

The Manager of Shipping must spend the office treasury until £2 or less remains. Available purchases are: lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3, without the shipyard owner's consent; or buy a Company ship for £5, but only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh. The summary does not specify a separate consent requirement for leasing or buying Company ships; owner consent is specifically waived for fitting a ship from a shipyard.

The President declares Trade regions including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die for every declared nonhome region, then roll the normal check. Failures may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. A President may have at most one successful Trade per turn. It must allow its Commander, Governors, and Trade their opportunities, and each position completes all actions before another begins; Trade may be ordered before or after the other positions but cannot interrupt one. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions. The first writer goes to the home port; each subsequent order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President may not fill another Presidency's home region, even if that other President's office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed revenue, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under Deregulation. The President gets £1 from the bank per order and each owner gets £1 per writer placed. Adjacent writers from different Presidencies are separated with dividers for return at Refresh.

A Commander may target their Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company-controlled target must have unrest or a closed order, so the Deploy can have an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once, while Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check; a noncatastrophic failure can be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, the owners roll one die for each officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for losses. A catastrophic failure returns the Commander to supply and returns half that family's trophies rounded up; exhausted officers still check losses, and no office card is vacated because Commanders have none.

On a successful Deploy, loot from the bank is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of the number of surviving officers used in this attempt plus one. Count only participating officers who survived this attempt and the regiments and alliance pieces used in it. Distribute each payout cycle in order: £1 to the Commander's family for the Commander plus £1 per their surviving used officer; then £1 per surviving used officer to other families clockwise; then £1 to the bank per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength. Stop a cycle when the cash runs out, then repeat the entire cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags. Open all orders and remove all unrest there. If the target was not already Company-controlled, create a Governorship by placing its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President's box, placing the Governor overlay on the map in the conquered region, and sending only the office card to Vacant Offices for later Hiring. Do not create Governors or overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in that conquered region facing outward, move it fully inside, threatening Rebellion. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — success payout/control; catastrophe

answers.answer: A Governor starts with the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one benefit: Build a Company ship, Commission a regiment, or Tax. Building takes two successful Build actions: if there is no partially built ship in the region, place one there; otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. A partially built ship has no other effect. Commissioning places a regiment in that President's Army; it has officer-like strength, pays loot to the bank, and does not roll for officer losses. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful attempt adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking dice pool until the Governor stops, has no dice remaining, or catastrophically fails.

During Company Revenue expenses, reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer and regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, increasing Debt one at a time to the track end and continuing to receive loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans reduce Standing one; three or more reduce it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under the current Standing; if it is below expectations, reduce Standing one. After this expectations check, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, at £1 per Company share, paying each owner £1 per share including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, Standing advances one. If Standing reaches its leftmost space, the Company fails; during Revenue go immediately to Final Scoring.

During a Crisis, resolve the attack at the Elephant's location, with its tail as attacker and head as target; the Event procedure then calls for the Elephant's March. If the attack is against a Company region, it also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks by Presidency order Bombay, Madras, Bengal, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Invasion/Rebellion against the Company has its normal attack strength plus unrest in the target; a Foreign Invasion primary uses only the ordinary attack die, without added unrest. A secondary Rebellion uses only that region's number of unrest cubes, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength or as much as possible, using alliances at printed strength and not splitting them. If newly exhausted defense is insufficient, perform Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that region and give the Commander one trophy; if that successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses pieces and gains or loses no trophies. This does not appoint a Commander. The summary describes ordering and strengths for attacks on Company regions; ordinary Crisis attack outcomes are: Invasion succeeds only if attacker's whole empire strength plus modifier is greater than defender's whole empire strength; Rebellion compares only the rebelling region's strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital and must be strictly greater. A failed Invasion removes one attacker tower; a failed Rebellion removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India — Crisis; Attacks on Company; Invasion Crisis; Rebellion Crisis

answers.answer: The PM selects a law and a matching policy and sets Vote marker to its printed starting support. Voting begins with the PM and proceeds clockwise; players spend £1 family cash per vote and may add printed card votes. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. Players may switch from support to opposition, but once opposing they cannot support during that vote. Opposition votes determine the Opposition Leader, with the current holder retaining a tie; votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose with that person's consent. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except under the forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise. At support −1 or less the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma's failure text if applicable, Opposition Leader takes the PM dial, and the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher the law passes: place it among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then the law's immediate effects. After either result, restore every voting card to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, with these exceptions and results: if it passes, reduce Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. There is no policy with this law; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated, so this session is not needed to activate firms there. The ordinary voting procedure supplies the vote threshold and mechanics; the summary does not enumerate any further exceptions beyond those specified.

In a deregulated Firms phase, after Family share creation and before Hiring, investments may be made in any order until nobody wants more; the manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms, then managers choose strategies. A player who currently manages no firm may form one by returning one eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to its invested side, flipping their family board, placing a family member as the first firm share, setting Value to the leftmost track space, and taking £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm requires manager consent and the same contribution of a Company share or workshop; it creates a firm share and puts £5 bank money into London. The ten-share maximum applies: investments beyond ten still contribute £5 but create no share. A Chairman share cannot be used; no Company share can be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and a Company share created this turn cannot be invested even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert, provide no bonus, and give no Company-failure VP, even if the firm fails. The ten-share cap applies to actual firm shares; excess contributions at the cap still add money. The firm money comes from the bank through the specified form/invest procedure, not family cash; family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments; cash location; ten-share limit

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose a trade zone/home port or Hobnob. A trade strategy requires at least one ship, permits a closed home port at selection, and commits a secret cash bid from London treasury; Hobnob has no bid, trade, or dividends, still pays expenses, and retains the previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategy cards facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before any actions, reveal matching strategies, roll one die per committed £1, and pay the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), potentially negative. A President that succeeds at Trade gets initiative calculated the same way using Presidency ships. After that success, fill in ascending initiative order; the President chooses the order among ties, with no automatic Company priority. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders and Governors have had their opportunity, and the Chairman chooses initiative ties. Each firm fills as many open orders as possible, up to ships plus one, starting at its strategy home port and tracing through its own filled route back there. It may fill each particular order only once, but can refill orders the Company or another firm filled that turn, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. Place filled tokens and put trade revenue in India treasury. Any previously filled order pays half its printed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for every full £6 added to its India treasury this turn.

At the start of Revenue, before Company expenses, firms pay in initiative order and then other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows and then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of firm share count or firm Value, and may be paid from either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, the firm dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends its shares to Debtor's Prison (each costs −1 VP), returns ships to shipyards and the charter to the family side; invested workshops remain invested. It may be rescued by emergency investments following normal Company-share/workshop rules—even if the ten-share limit prevents more shares, the firm still gets the investment money; use it to pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment—or by merging with one other firm. In the latter case, the other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already and cover the failing firm's unpaid expenses. After expenses the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend costs £1 per firm share plus £1 for the manager; with manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on a dividend. Record the total actual cash paid out on the Company Balance track as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep the remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in their strategy zone, except Hobnob ships are exempt.
